chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Joining Louis Armstrong's band: lineup and rehearsal
summary: Armstrong sends for Budd via Mac McKendrick; Budd lists Z. T. Randolph, Stump Evans, Keg, the Oldham brothers, Teddy Wilson and Yank Porter.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So anyway, while we were all living at Mrs. Otter's Mike S/ Louis Armstrong sent for us. We got a call from Mac McKendricks. Mac McKendricks was the band leader, the straw boss.
And he played tenor banjo, the four-string banjo. And so when we went to rehearsal, that first rehearsal is when we met Z. T. Randolph, who was the musical director.
And we had Stump -- Stump Evans in the band. Was it Evans? Or Stump Smith?
And -- on trumpet. Z. T. on trumpet, and Louis was of course playing his trumpet, and singing, and my brother, Keg Johnson on trombone, and then we had the Oldham brothers.
George played the alto, and his other brother played the bass.
Bill? Oldham played the bass. And we had Teddy Wilson on piano, and they sent for Yank Porter on drums. And --

Yank was in New York. I think he had -- he was with the second -- with the -- one of the revived Black Birds show, and so Pop sent for Yank to join the band in New York, and Yank came, and we -- he was a pretty good drummer, see. So anyway, Yank played in the band. We went on tour.
